title: Pendulum Truck Collision Lab
description: A giant Rolex watch hangs from the ceiling as a pendulum bob, while a CesiumMilkTruck sits on a frictionless track below. The user configures pendulum release angles, truck mass multipliers, and restitution coefficients, then releases the pendulum to collide with the truck, observing momentum and energy conservation across multiple coupled trials with full undo/redo support.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) implementing a pendulum-collision physics lab. Load CesiumMilkTruck.glb and rolex.glb using GLTFLoader. Scene setup: a ground plane with grid texture as a frictionless track, a vertical support frame (thin box geometry pillars and crossbar) centered above. The Rolex model is attached to the crossbar by a visible rope (CylinderGeometry) forming a pendulum, scaled so it acts as the bob. The MilkTruck sits on the track at the pendulum's rest position. Camera: OrbitControls, initial perspective at 45 degrees, distance 12 units. Lighting: ambient light plus two directional lights with soft shadows enabled on the renderer. UI panel (HTML overlay, left side): sliders for pendulum release angle (10-80 degrees), truck mass multiplier (0.5x-3.0x), coefficient of restitution (0.0-1.0), and a checkbox to toggle gravity strength (9.8 or 4.9 m/s²). Buttons: Release, Reset, Undo, Redo. Interaction flow (10-14 steps): user adjusts release angle, sets truck mass, sets restitution, optionally toggles gravity, clicks Release. The pendulum swings down under gravity, the Rolex bob strikes the truck. On collision, compute post-collision velocities using 1D conservation of momentum and the restitution coefficient. Animate the truck sliding along the track and the pendulum rebounding. Display a real-time HUD showing kinetic energy, potential energy, total energy, and momentum for both objects, updating each frame during animation. After each trial, log results in a scrollable history list below the sliders. Undo reverts the last parameter change or trial, restoring previous state including object positions and logged results. Redo re-applies. After the collision animation completes, highlight in green or red whether total momentum was conserved within 1% tolerance. Allow the user to chain multiple trials without full reset, accumulating the truck's position from prior collisions. Reset returns everything to initial state and clears history.
